chapters.title: One Person, Many Hands
chapters.tease: Agents supply the hands; you supply the order. The habits around one person make the machine.

chapters.title: The Day Is the Machine
chapters.tease: Your working day, not your tools, is the machine: review, sessions, close.

chapters.title: Doing Versus Deciding
chapters.tease: Agents take over the doing. The deciding does not shrink; it grows, and it is now your job.

chapters.title: The Three Operator Questions
chapters.tease: Every task must survive three questions: what do we want, why now, and how will I know?

chapters.title: Throughput Is Not the Point
chapters.tease: Agents give you volume. Count what crossed the line, not what you started.

chapters.title: Direct, No Preamble
chapters.tease: Agents need no warm-up. Say what you want, how you will judge it, then stop. Ask the same of them.

chapters.title: Bias to Action, Bound by Evidence
chapters.tease: Act as fast as you like, as long as every move leaves evidence you actually check.

chapters.title: Artifact First
chapters.tease: When in doubt, make the thing. A rough version now costs less than the meeting about it.

chapters.title: The Small Machine Rule
chapters.tease: Keep the whole system small enough to hold in your head on a tired Thursday afternoon.

chapters.title: The Name on the Door
chapters.tease: However capable the agents, your name is on the door. Delegate the effort; keep the ownership.

chapters.title: The Shape of a Good Day
chapters.tease: A good day is three strokes: a short review, a middle of sessions, and a short close.

chapters.title: The Morning Review
chapters.tease: Twenty minutes of triage: look wide, narrow to decisions, choose today's outcomes. Then start.

chapters.title: Reading What Ran Overnight
chapters.tease: Read overnight work before its summary, check the evidence, then ship, resend or park it.

chapters.title: Choosing Today's Three
chapters.tease: Pick three outcomes a day, each visibly finished by the close: high impact, moderate effort.

chapters.title: Time-Blocked Sessions
chapters.tease: A session has one purpose: it starts with a brief, ends with a decision, and contains nothing else.

chapters.title: Starting a Session Cleanly
chapters.tease: The first five minutes of a session decide most of the next hour. Start clean.

chapters.title: The Middle of the Day
chapters.tease: While agents run, do not hover. Check in, unblock what waits on you, then step away.

chapters.title: Interrupts and the Queue
chapters.tease: Every interrupt meets one question. Almost always the answer is no, and it goes to the queue.

chapters.title: The Finish Command
chapters.tease: End every session with the same ritual: verify, ship, note, stop. Five minutes.

chapters.title: Closing the Day
chapters.tease: The close is twenty minutes that start tomorrow: shipped, still open, tomorrow, stop.

chapters.title: A Brief Is a Contract
chapters.tease: Treat a brief as a contract both sides can check: goal, context, constraints and done.

chapters.title: Start With Done
chapters.tease: Write the definition of done before the task. It is where your judgement lives.

chapters.title: Context, Not Biography
chapters.tease: Give the context the task needs and the agent cannot find, and no more. Context, not biography.

chapters.title: Constraints Are a Kindness
chapters.tease: Constraints are not a lack of trust. They tell the agent where the task ends, so it can focus.

chapters.title: Name the Files, Name the Checks
chapters.tease: Replace descriptions with pointers: the file path, the example, the exact check to run.

chapters.title: The One-Paragraph Brief
chapters.tease: Most briefs fit in one paragraph. If yours runs to a page, the thinking is not finished.

chapters.title: Flag the Deviation
chapters.tease: When an agent must depart from the brief, it should say so at the top, and you make the call.

chapters.title: Examples Beat Adjectives
chapters.tease: Adjectives are the weakest words in a brief. Replace them with real examples wherever you can.

chapters.title: Briefs That Outlive the Session
chapters.tease: When you write the same brief a third time, it is a recipe. Write it down properly and keep it.

chapters.title: The Library of Recipes
chapters.tease: Gather your recipes into one plain-text library, sorted into families. Check it before writing any brief.

chapters.title: Memory Is Infrastructure
chapters.tease: Agents start each session knowing nothing. Written memory is infrastructure, like plumbing.

chapters.title: What the Agent Should Already Know
chapters.tease: A short memory file answers a newcomer's first questions: purpose, commands, rules and pitfalls.

chapters.title: The Operator's Notebook
chapters.tease: Keep one running notebook for the whole operation, one line per thing, and re-read it to decide.

chapters.title: A Decision Log
chapters.tease: Log each significant decision: date, the decision, the reason, and the alternative you rejected.

chapters.title: Notes That Get Read
chapters.tease: What matters is not how much you write, but how much is read again and changes a decision.

chapters.title: Pruning the Memory
chapters.tease: Memory only grows unless you prune it. Stale memory is worse than none: agents act on it confidently.

chapters.title: One Source of Truth
chapters.tease: Every fact should have exactly one home. Everywhere else, point to it.

chapters.title: Secrets Stay Out
chapters.tease: Memory is not a vault. Anything an agent reads daily will eventually be seen widely.

chapters.title: Session Handoffs
chapters.tease: A four-question handoff, drafted by the agent and corrected by you, lets the next session start fast.

chapters.title: The Filing Cabinet Mind
chapters.tease: Skip the second brain. Build a simple filing cabinet that opens at the right drawer.

chapters.title: The Project Register
chapters.tease: One register lists every project, one line each, with a status and a next move.

chapters.title: One Line Per Project
chapters.tease: Each register line is name, status, next move and date. If you cannot write it, you cannot steer it.

chapters.title: Status Words That Mean Something
chapters.tease: Use a few status words, each implying an action: idea, active, parked, done, and perhaps waiting.

chapters.title: Parking Without Guilt
chapters.tease: If a project cannot move meaningfully this week, park it on purpose, with a note and a condition.

chapters.title: Threads Are Units of Delegation
chapters.tease: A thread is not a chat window. It is a bounded job: a brief, a scope, checks and a handoff.

chapters.title: One Thread, One Outcome
chapters.tease: Each thread should aim at exactly one outcome, so it can be reviewed, shipped and reverted alone.

chapters.title: Parallel, Not Tangled
chapters.tease: Parallel agents help only when each has its own territory and results arrive one at a time.

chapters.title: Handing Off Well
chapters.tease: A good handoff is a short exchange: brief, questions and a plan back, confirmation, then work.

chapters.title: When to Pull a Thread Back
chapters.tease: Threads drift. Spot it early, pull back as hard as the drift requires, then fix the cause upstream.

chapters.title: The Coordinator's Seat
chapters.tease: Coordinating means dividing an outcome into slices, reviewing each, and making the joins fit.

chapters.title: Review Is the Job
chapters.tease: When agents do the making, review is where your judgement touches the work. It is the job, not a chore.

chapters.title: Evidence Over Reassurance
chapters.tease: Reassurance is a claim; evidence is something you can check. Ask for the receipt, not the promise.

chapters.title: Read the Diff, Not the Summary
chapters.tease: Agent summaries are excellent and written by the party that did the work. Read the diff first.

chapters.title: The Cheapest Check First
chapters.tease: Order your checks by cost, cheapest first, and stop as soon as you have enough confidence for the risk.

chapters.title: The Two-Pass Review
chapters.tease: Review in two passes: shape first, then detail. Work with the wrong shape never earns a line edit.

chapters.title: What Green Hides
chapters.tease: Green tells you the checks passed, not that they were the right checks. Trouble hides in the overlap.

chapters.title: Reviewing Prose and Pictures
chapters.tease: Prose and pictures have no test suite, yet they are what other people see. Review them harder, not softer.

chapters.title: Comments That Teach
chapters.tease: Comments should fix this draft and the next. Specific, explained and portable, then promoted to memory.

chapters.title: Redo or Repair
chapters.tease: Right shape, repair it. Wrong shape, or two failed rounds, redo it with a better brief.

chapters.title: Taste Is a Review Skill
chapters.tease: Correct is the floor and good is common. Yours is the narrowest filter, and only you can apply it.

chapters.title: Ship Small, Ship Often
chapters.tease: Small changes, each reviewed and released on its own, in a steady stream. Not a nervous lump.

chapters.title: The Pull Request as Paper Trail
chapters.tease: A pull request is a gate and a paper trail: a searchable record of what changed, why and on what evidence.

chapters.title: Automerge and Its Conditions
chapters.tease: Automerge suits low-risk changes with strong checks. Everything else waits for a human merge.

chapters.title: Checks You Trust
chapters.tease: What matters is not how many checks you have but how many would actually fail if something went wrong.

chapters.title: Versioned Passes
chapters.tease: Do large work in numbered passes, each with one purpose, each reviewed for one kind of problem and kept.

chapters.title: Ship Beats Perfect, Mostly
chapters.tease: Ship beats perfect when undo is cheap. When undo is costly, more polish is prudence, not perfectionism.

chapters.title: The Release Note
chapters.tease: Every release gets a four-line note: what, why, risk and undo. Two minutes, almost always skipped.

chapters.title: Rollback Is a Feature
chapters.tease: An operation that can roll back in a minute can ship boldly. Roll back first, investigate second.

chapters.title: Never Commit Secrets
chapters.tease: The one rule that is not a default: never commit secrets. Not to code, memory, briefs or notes.

chapters.title: Done Means Live
chapters.tease: Done means live, in front of the people it was for, and checked there. Merged is only a milestone.

chapters.title: The Weekly Review
chapters.tease: Once a week, step back for an hour: gather, review, decide, plan. The deciding is the heart of it.

chapters.title: Clearing the Decks
chapters.tease: Once a week, take every open loop and close, decide, park or drop it. Leave nothing undecided.

chapters.title: Counting What Shipped
chapters.tease: Count what shipped, live and checked, every week. The gaps between the layers show where work sticks.

chapters.title: The Quarterly Review
chapters.tease: Every quarter, read the record, then ask of everything: keep, end, start or change?

chapters.title: Killing Projects Kindly
chapters.tease: Ask whether a project is still worth what it costs. If not, end it well: close, note, archive, tell.

chapters.title: Energy Is the Real Budget
chapters.tease: Agents can work any hours. Your limit is energy: the quality of attention you bring to deciding and reviewing.

chapters.title: Attention Has a Ceiling
chapters.tease: You could run fifty threads. You can properly review a few. That smaller number is your real capacity.

chapters.title: The Hours You Are Good For
chapters.tease: Nobody is good for eight hours of judgement. Find your deep hours and give them the deep work.

chapters.title: Rest Is Maintenance
chapters.tease: Rest is not a reward for finishing. It is maintenance for the judgement that runs everything.

chapters.title: A Pace You Can Keep
chapters.tease: A pace you can keep beats a pace that impresses, because steady habits compound and bursts oscillate.

chapters.title: Fewer Tools, Better Kept
chapters.tease: A small toolbelt you know deeply beats a large one you know shallowly. Be slow to adopt, quick to drop.

chapters.title: The Toolbelt Audit
chapters.tease: Tools pile up silently. Each quarter, list everything, check its use and access, then keep, change or remove.

chapters.title: Upkeep Is Scheduled
chapters.tease: Upkeep left unscheduled happens never or in a crisis. Schedule it, do it, then verify it worked.

chapters.title: Permissions as Policy
chapters.tease: Decide once what agents may do freely, must ask about, and may never do. Write it down and enforce it.

chapters.title: Fragile Wins Cost More
chapters.tease: Hacks win today and fail later, silently, on the worst day. Aim for fast enough and robust enough.

chapters.title: Mistakes Are Data
chapters.tease: Every mistake is data. Fix it, then ask why, and the upstream cause stops producing the next one.

chapters.title: The Incident Note
chapters.tease: A fifteen-minute note: what happened, why, and what changes. Most of the time goes on the why.

chapters.title: Blameless, Even Alone
chapters.tease: Blamelessness matters most when the only person to blame is you. Look at the system, not the nearest person.

chapters.title: Guardrails From Scars
chapters.tease: The best guardrails are learned: a scar becomes a lesson, and the lesson becomes something in the system.

chapters.title: The Runbook Habit
chapters.tease: Done it twice and will do it again? Write the runbook: steps, a check after each, and how to undo it.

chapters.title: The Decision Queue
chapters.tease: Tasks can be delegated; decisions cannot. The decision queue is what the operation is really waiting on.

chapters.title: One-Way and Two-Way Doors
chapters.tease: Two-way doors can be walked back through, so decide them fast. One-way doors deserve care.

chapters.title: Saying No to Good Ideas
chapters.tease: Bad ideas are easy to decline. The skill is saying not yet to good ones, so that something gets finished.

chapters.title: Deciding on Partial Evidence
chapters.tease: Complete evidence rarely arrives. Decide where more evidence is worth less than the cost of waiting.

chapters.title: The Price of Not Deciding
chapters.tease: Not deciding is a decision made by default. Drift closes options until something else chooses for you.

chapters.title: Judgement Does Not Delegate
chapters.tease: Agents keep climbing the stack of work. The top layers, what good means and why it matters, stay yours.

chapters.title: Teach What You Run
chapters.tease: Writing down how your operation works, clearly enough for someone else, shows you what you actually do.

chapters.title: The Operator Ahead
chapters.tease: Agents take the middle of the work. The edges, stating intent and exercising judgement, become the job.

chapters.title: The Handbook as Habit
chapters.tease: A handbook is for using, not finishing: read when relevant, practise, revise, a practice or two at a time.

chapters.title: The Job Is Deciding
chapters.tease: The operator's real job is deciding, not doing. Everything else is machinery for deciding well.
